accepted.question_text: For every real number epsilon > 0, if m is a sufficiently large even integer and A is a set of distinct reduced residue classes modulo m with |A| > (1/2 + epsilon) phi(m), must the sumset A + A contain almost all even residue classes modulo m?
accepted.context_brief: Sarkozy Problem 66a on binary sumsets modulo m

evidence.quote: Problem 66. Is it true, that if epsilon > 0, m in N, m is even, m -> infinity, and A is a set of distinct modulo m reduced residue classes with |A| > (1/2 + epsilon) phi(m), then a) A + A contains almost all even residue classes modulo m;
Theorem 1. The answers to Problem 66 a) and b) are both negative.

accepted.question_text: For every real number epsilon > 0, if m is a sufficiently large even integer and A is a set of distinct reduced residue classes modulo m with |A| > (1/2 + epsilon) phi(m), must the triple sumset A + A + A contain every odd residue class modulo m?
accepted.context_brief: Sarkozy Problem 66b on ternary sumsets modulo m

evidence.quote: Problem 66. Is it true, that if epsilon > 0, m in N, m is even, m -> infinity, and A is a set of distinct modulo m reduced residue classes with |A| > (1/2 + epsilon) phi(m), then b) A + A + A contains every odd residue class modulo m?
Theorem 1. The answers to Problem 66 a) and b) are both negative.

accepted.question_text: If Q = {q1, q2, ...} is an infinite set of primes satisfying lim inf_{x -> infinity} (log x / x) |{qi : qi <= x, qi in Q}| > 1/2, does every sufficiently large odd integer 2n + 1 admit a representation qi + qj + qk = 2n + 1 with qi, qj, qk in Q?
accepted.context_brief: Sarkozy Problem 67 on ternary sums from dense prime subsets

evidence.quote: Problem 67. Is it true that if Q = {q1, q2, . . .} is an infinite set of primes such that lim inf x->infinity (log x / x) |{qi : qi <= x, qi in Q}| > 1/2, then every large odd integer 2n + 1 can be represented in the form qi + qj + qk = 2n + 1 (with qi, qj, qk in Q)?
In [20] Yang and Togbe answered negatively Problem 67 and obtained more explicit results on this problem.

Theorem 2. There is an infinite set Q of primes with upper relative prime density 1 and lower relative prime density 5/8 such that there are infinitely many odd integers 2n + 1 that cannot be represented as q1 + q2 + q3 = 2n + 1 with qi in Q (1 <= i <= 3).
